result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. Riley got 3 items correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback in short |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only outputs a tool request with its arguments. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | "It will eventually fix the bug" is wrong: the agent is repeating the same failure, so it needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | 4 is right, but the reasoning says the model runs the tools itself. The program runs them, and the model is called once for the question and once for each of the three results. |
| q5 | correct | Riley gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide what to do next. |
| q6 | partial | The name is only part of it. The model also reads each tool's description and parameters. |

Riley has the loop and the tool-request idea down. Two things still need work: the program, not the model, runs the tools (q4), and a loop needs a stopping condition (q3). I also added learning record `0003-who-runs-tools-and-when-to-stop.md` and updated `NOTES.md`; s1 is still ungraded.

**Next step:** sketch one makerspace request on paper, marking which steps are model output and which are program actions, and where a step limit would stop the loop if a tool kept failing. Then write a one-sentence description for `check_calendar`.

Do you want me to grade s1 as well, so we can compare the two attempts?
